column1: # Defines whose target class is not a supported class (#239).
# docs/target-classes.md states the boundary the v1.0 criterion hangs off:
# "supported classes are exactly the rows of the first table below
# (Measured, with verdicts). The refusal tables and the Rust narrative are
# not supported classes, whatever verdicts their stories contain."
# The A-group is a rate over supported-class targets, so a committed define
# whose target sits in a refusal table is outside the corpus — not because
# it refused, but because its class has no recorded verdict at all. That
# distinction matters in both directions: watson also refuses and IS in the
# corpus, because its class (Python CLI) is a first-table row. Refusal is
# not the criterion; the class is.
# These targets were not superseded by anything — no later revision exists
# that reaches a verdict — so they do not belong in supersession.tsv, and
# count.py check keeps the two files from absorbing each other's rows.
# Columns (tab-separated):
#   define  refusal_table_row  reason
# refusal_table_row is the Class cell of the docs/target-classes.md row
# this define's target appears under, quoted verbatim.
